deed: רב אשי ורבינא ערכו את התלמוד הבבלי
year: 352–427, שנות חייו של רב אשי לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית
title: Rav Ashi and Ravina gathered the teachings of the Babylonian sages and edited the Babylonian Talmud

trailer.text: According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Rav Ashi (352–427) was a celebrated Babylonian amora who reestablished the academy at Sura and was the first editor of the Babylonian Talmud.
According to Chabad, Rav Ashi was the leader of the Jewish people, and according to the Jewish Encyclopedia he made Sura the spiritual center of the Babylonian Jews.
According to Chabad, he wove together the teachings of more than 500 scholars.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the work he began was continued for two generations and completed by Rabina, head of the academy in Sura.
According to Chabad, the Jewish people accepted the Babylonian Talmud as the final halachic authority.

stations.title: Before: scattered teachings and divided academies

paragraphs.text: According to Chabad, the first major Talmudic seminary in Babylon was founded by Rav.
According to Chabad, Rav Huna and Rav Chisda could not come to an agreement, and Rav Chisda left the academy.
This was a great blow to the standing of Sura.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the Sura academy had been closed since the death of Ḥisda in 309.
According to Chabad, two years after the death of Shmuel the city of Neherda’a was destroyed by a band of brigands, and it was never restored.
According to Chabad, it seems that a process of fragmentation began, in which great scholars established academies of their own instead of gathering in one central location.

According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, in 351 the Roman commander Ursicinus took vengeance on the Jews of Tiberias, Sepphoris and Lydda, the beginning of the end of organized Jewish learning in the Land of Israel.
According to Chabad, the Talmudic material was not written down at first.
According to Rashi, as quoted in a Chabad article, until the days of Rav Ashi and Ravina there was no Gemara arranged in order.
Each one stated his reasoning when a question was asked in the study hall.

stations.title: Rav Ashi and his academy in Sura

paragraphs.text: According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Simai, Rav Ashi's father, was a rich and learned man.
He was a student of the academy at Naresh, near Sura, which was headed by Papa, Raba's disciple.
According to Chabad, Rav Ashi had three qualities: political power from the Babylonian authorities, recognition as a great Torah scholar, and wealth.
According to Chabad, it helped him that he was wealthy and that he lived a long life.
According to Chabad, perhaps his most notable quality was his ability to unite the greatest minds.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Rav Ashi rebuilt Rab's academy and the synagogue beside it, sparing no expense and supervising the work personally.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, under Rav Ashi the Sura academy regained all its former importance.
According to Chabad, for two hundred years no academy reached the heights of Sura in the days of Rav, until Rav Ashi, whose academy was in Mata Mechasiya, a suburb of Sura.

stations.title: The deed: gathering the sages and arranging the Gemara

paragraphs.text: According to Chabad, Rav Ashi made a point over several decades of befriending the scholars of all the academies in Babylon.
According to Chabad, twice a year, for an entire month, tens of thousands of scholars gathered in Mata Mechasiya to study.
According to Chabad, the Talmud (Gittin, folio nun-tet, side aleph) states that from the days of Rebbi until Rav Ashi there was no time when all the Torah sages were gathered in one place.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Rav Ashi made it the labor of his life to collect the explanations of the Mishnah, after critical scrutiny, under the name "Gemara."
According to Rashi, Rav Ashi and Ravina arranged the traditions of the amoraim who preceded them and set them in the order of the tractates, beside the appropriate Mishnah.
According to Chabad, Rav Ashi wove together the teachings of more than 500 scholars.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, he completed the work together with his disciples and the scholars who gathered in Sura for the Kallah.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, what is probably historical in the traditional account is that Rav Ashi revised the work twice.
According to Chabad, there was a first draft and a final copy.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the kindly attitude of King Yezdegerd I greatly favored the undertaking.
The recognition of Rav Ashi's authority by the academies of Nehardea and Pumbedita also helped.
According to a Chabad article, the situation of the Jews in the Sasanian Empire was generally favorable.
According to Chabad, Rav Ashi died in 426, and Ravina II continued the final editing.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the work was continued for two generations and completed by Rabina, head of the academy in Sura.
According to Chabad, the Talmud went from oral arrangement by Abaye and Rava, to major writing by Rav Ashi, to final halachos by Ravina II.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Tavyomi, Rav Ashi's son, was invested with his father's position only in 455, twenty-eight years after his father's death.
According to Maimonides, Rav Ashi composed the Gemara, and it was completed in the days of his son.

stations.title: The result: a book on which Judaism rests

paragraphs.text: According to Chabad, the Talmud consists of 2,711 folios, or 5,422 pages, mostly in dense, cryptic text.
According to Chabad, there were two Talmuds, Jerusalem and Babylonian, and they are very different works.
According to Maimonides, the greatness of the work and its immense benefit are faithful testimony to it.
According to Rabbi Yitzchak Isaac HaLevi, as quoted in a Chabad article, the entire Talmud, as it is before us, follows the arrangement of Rav Ashi and his circle.
According to Chabad, the Jewish people accepted the Babylonian Talmud as the final halachic authority.
According to a Chabad article, the Talmud was accepted as the authoritative and sole source of all halacha.
According to Chabad, Judaism as we know it would be unimaginable without the Talmud.

stations.title: "Rav Ashi and Ravina are the end of instruction"

paragraphs.text: According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the saying that Rav Ashi and Rabina are the end of instruction is an evident reference to their work in editing the Babylonian Talmud.

According to a Chabad article, Rav Ashi and Ravina are the sealers of the Talmud in the sense that after them the halakhic sages had no authority to introduce new laws and lines of reasoning that are not founded entirely on traditions received precisely through transmission from the earlier Amoraim.
According to Maimonides, Ravina and Rav Ashi and their colleagues were the last of the great sages of Israel who transmitted the Oral Torah.
According to Maimonides, after the court of Rav Ashi the Jewish people dispersed across many lands.

According to the Kesef Mishneh, by Rabbi Joseph Karo, it is possible that from the day the Talmud was sealed it was accepted that later generations would not dispute earlier ones, as with the sealing of the Mishnah.
According to Richard Kalmin (1986), the question of the redaction of the Talmud, the final stages in the shaping of the document, is a problem every student of the Talmud must face.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, there is no statement in the Talmud itself that makes it possible to decide whether the editorial work was written down in the days of Rav Ashi.
According to Kalmin, in his earlier work Albeck accepted the traditional view of Rav Ashi's unique role in the final editing.
According to Kalmin, Halivni notes that the period between the death of Rav Ashi and the death of the later Ravina is approximately one-third of the amoraic period.
According to Kalmin, Halivni claims that the material which can be dated with certainty to the period after Rav Ashi is less than 5 percent of the amoraic contribution to the Talmud.
According to Chabad, the additions of the Savoraim to the Babylonian Talmud are less than 2% of the text.
According to a Chabad article, at the end of the amoraic period, at the end of the reign of Yezdegerd II, there was a significant deterioration for the Jews.
According to a Chabad article, King Peroz I decreed the execution of three of the leaders of the Jewish community, among them the Exilarch.
According to Kalmin, it appears that the rabbis suffered some sort of persecution at the hands of the Persians in the period after Rav Ashi.
According to Kalmin, all of the Jewish sources on the persecutions were composed hundreds of years after the events.
According to Kalmin, Geonic sources state that the persecutions did not begin until 455.
According to a Chabad article, after the death of the last Ravina, the Sura academy declined.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, רב אשי היה אמורא בבלי מפורסם (352–427), שחידש את ישיבת סורא והיה העורך הראשון של התלמוד הבבלי.
claims.quote: A celebrated Babylonian amora; born 352; died 427; reestablished the academy at Sura, and was the first editor of the Babylonian Talmud.

claims.text: לפי חב"ד, רב אשי, מנהיג העם היהודי, היה בעל שלוש תכונות: כוח מדיני מהשלטונות הבבליים, הכרה כגדול תורה וכן עושר.
claims.quote: Rav Ashi, the leader of the Jewish people, had the three qualities necessary for this endeavor: supreme political power granted him by the Babylonian authorities,

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, רב אשי הפך את סורא למרכז הרוחני של יהודי בבל.
claims.quote: Ashi not only elevated Sura till it became the intellectual center of the Babylonian Jews, but contributed to its material grandeur also.

claims.text: לפי חב"ד, רב אשי שזר את תורתם של יותר מ-500 חכמים.
claims.quote: He wove the teachings of more than 500 scholars into an intricate tapestry

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, המפעל שהחל רב אשי נמשך שני דורות והושלם בידי רבינא, ראש ישיבת סורא, שמת ב-499.
claims.quote: The work begun by Ashi was continued by the two succeeding generations, and completed by Rabina, another president of the college in Sura, who died in 499.

claims.text: לפי חב"ד, העם היהודי קיבל אז את התלמוד הבבלי כסמכות ההלכתית הסופית.
claims.quote: At that point, the Jewish people accepted that the Babylonian Talmud, composed of the Mishnah and the Gemara, was the final halachic authority.

claims.text: לפי מאמר באתר חב"ד בעברית, העריכה הגדולה והמסכמת של התלמוד הבבלי נעשתה בידי רב אשי ורבינא.

claims.quote: עריכת התלמוד נעשתה בישיבת סורא – מתא מחסיא – על ידי רבינא ורב אשי.

claims.text: לפי חב"ד, התלמוד כולל 2,711 דפים (5,422 עמודים), רובם בטקסט צפוף וסתום.
claims.quote: It consists of 2,711 folios, or 5,422 pages, mostly written in dense, cryptic text.

claims.text: לפי הרמב"ם, רבינא ורב אשי וחבריהם היו סוף גדולי חכמי ישראל המעתיקים תורה שבעל פה.
claims.quote: נמצא רבינא ורב אשי וחבריהם סוף גדולי חכמי ישראל המעתיקים תורה שבעל-פה

claims.text: לפי הכסף משנה (רבי יוסף קארו), כמו שבחתימת המשנה, אפשר שמיום חתימת התלמוד התקבל שדורות אחרונים לא יחלקו על הראשונים.
claims.quote: ואפשר לאמור שמיום חתימת המשנה קיימו וקיבלו שדורות האחרונים לא יחלקו על הראשונים

claims.text: לפי ריצ'רד קלמין (1986), שאלת עריכת התלמוד, השלבים האחרונים בעיצוב המסמך, היא בעיה שכל לומד תלמוד חייב להתמודד איתה.
claims.quote: The problem of the redaction of the Talmud, the final stages of the process by which the document before us assumed its present shape, is one which every student of the Talmud must eventually face.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, אין בתלמוד עצמו אמירה שמאפשרת להכריע אם העריכה נכתבה בימי רב אשי.
claims.quote: Even the question as to whether this editorial work was written down, and thus, whether the putting of the Babylonian Talmud into writing took place under Ashi or not

claims.text: לפי קלמין, בעבודתו המוקדמת קיבל אלבק את הדעה המסורתית על תפקידו הייחודי של רב אשי בעריכה הסופית.
claims.quote: However, in Albeck's earlier work, he accepts the traditional view of Rav Ashi's unique role in the final editing of the Talmud.

claims.text: לפי קלמין, הליבני מציין שהתקופה בין מות רב אשי ב-427 למות רבינא המאוחר ב-501 היא כשליש מתקופת האמוראים.
claims.quote: in 427 and the death of the later Ravina in 501 represents approximately one-third of the total duration of the amoraic period

claims.text: לפי קלמין, הליבני טוען שהחומר שאפשר לתארך בוודאות לתקופה שאחרי רב אשי הוא פחות מ-5 אחוז מתרומת האמוראים לתלמוד.
claims.quote: claims that the material which can be dated with certainty to this period adds up to less than 5 percent of the total amoraic contribution to the Talmud.

claims.text: לפי חב"ד, תוספות הסבוראים לתלמוד הבבלי מהוות פחות מ-2% מהטקסט.
claims.quote: In all, the Rabanan Savoroi’s total additions to the Babylonian Talmud comprise less than 2% of the text.

claims.text: לפי מאמר חב"ד, בסוף תקופת האמוראים, בסוף שלטון יזדגרד השני, התחוללה הרעה משמעותית ליהודים.
claims.quote: אולם בסוף ימי האמוראים התחוללה הרעה משמעותית ליהודים - בסוף שלטונו של יזדגרד השני.

claims.text: לפי מאמר חב"ד, המלך פירוז הראשון גזר להרוג שלושה מראשי הקהילה היהודית, ובהם ראש הגולה.
claims.quote: הלה, בין היתר, גזר על הוצאתם להורג של שלושה מראשי הקהילה היהודית - ראש הגולה

claims.text: לפי קלמין, נראה שהחכמים סבלו מרדיפה כלשהי מצד הפרסים בתקופה שאחרי רב אשי.
claims.quote: It does appear that the rabbis suffered some sort of persecution at the hands of the Persians during this period.

claims.text: לפי קלמין, כל המקורות היהודיים על הרדיפות נכתבו מאות שנים אחרי האירועים.
claims.quote: However, it should be noted that all of the relevant Jewish sources were composed several hundred years after the events they describe.

claims.text: לפי קלמין, מקורות גאוניים קובעים שהרדיפות לא החלו עד שנת 455.
claims.quote: according to which the persecutions did not begin until 455 C.E.

claims.text: לפי מאמר חב"ד, רבינא האחרון נפטר בשנת 474, ואחריו חלה ירידה בישיבת סורא.
claims.quote: אולם אחרי פטירתו של רבינא האחרון בשנת ד'רל"ד (474)

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, כהונתו של רב אשי בראשות ישיבת סורא נמשכה כנראה חמישים ושתיים שנה.
claims.quote: A particularly important element in Ashi's success was the length of his tenure of office as head of the Sura Academy, which must have lasted fifty-two years,

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, המסורת הגזימה, כנראה לשם עיגול, ל-60 שנות כהונה.
claims.quote: but which tradition, probably for the sake of round numbers, has exaggerated into sixty.

claims.text: לפי חב"ד, עריכת התלמוד נמשכה כמה דורות אחרי רב אשי, אך הוא יצר את הגוף העיקרי.
claims.quote: The process of editing the Talmud continued for several generations after Rav Ashi, but he created the main body.

claims.text: לפי מאמר חב"ד, התלמוד המשיך להיערך ולהשתכלל עד סוף ימי הסבוראים.
claims.quote: למעשה, התלמוד עדיין היה בתהליך של עריכה ושל שיכלול וזאת עד סוף ימי הסבוראים.

claims.text: לפי פלדבלום, כפי שמצוטט אצל קלמין, הדעה הרבנית הרווחת היא שהתלמוד נערך עריכה אחידה שהושלמה עד סוף המאה החמישית.
claims.quote: The prevalent Rabbinic view … assumes a uniform redaction of the Talmud completed by the close of the fifth century

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, בשנת 351 נקם המפקד הרומי אורסיקינוס ביהודי טבריה, ציפורי ולוד, וזו הייתה תחילת סופו של הלימוד התורני המאורגן בארץ ישראל.
claims.quote: the Roman commander Ursicinus wreaked vengeance on the Jews of Tiberias, Sepphoris, and Lydda

quote_translations.c50: The editing of the Talmud was done in the Sura academy – Mata Mechasiya – by Ravina and Rav Ashi.
quote_translations.c40: Until their days [of Rav Ashi and Ravina] there was no Gemara in order; rather, when a question was asked about the reasoning of the Mishnah in the study hall
quote_translations.c41: And Rav Ashi and Ravina arranged the traditions of the amoraim who preceded them, and set them in the order of the tractates, each one beside the Mishnah that is fitting and taught for it
quote_translations.c47: The situation of the Jews in the Sasanian Empire was generally favorable
quote_translations.c44: And after the court of Rav Ashi, who composed the Gemara, and it was completed in the days of his son, Israel was dispersed throughout all the lands in a great dispersion
quote_translations.c42: When Rav Ashi completed the composition of the Talmud as it is before us, the greatness of his composition was
quote_translations.c54: The entire Talmud as it is before us is according to the arrangement of Rav Ashi and his circle in his days
quote_translations.c45: The Talmud was accepted as the authoritative and sole source of all halacha.
quote_translations.c53: That is to say, Rav Ashi and Ravina are the sealers of the Talmud in the sense that after them authority was no longer given to the halachic sages
quote_translations.c43: It follows that Ravina and Rav Ashi and their colleagues were the last of the great sages of Israel who transmitted the Oral Torah
quote_translations.c46: And it is possible to say that from the day the Mishnah was sealed they established and accepted that the later generations would not dispute the earlier ones
quote_translations.c48: However, at the end of the days of the amoraim a significant deterioration occurred for the Jews - at the end of the reign of Yezdegerd II.
quote_translations.c49: He, among other things, decreed the execution of three of the leaders of the Jewish community - the Exilarch
quote_translations.c51: However, after the death of the last Ravina in the year dalet-resh-lamed-dalet (474)
quote_translations.c52: In fact, the Talmud was still in a process of editing and refinement, and this until the end of the days of the Savoraim.
